title: Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025
body: News Release Explore Product View News Release Related Materials Contacts EMBARGOED UNTIL RELEASE AT 10:00 a.m. EST, Wednesday, November 18, 2026 BEA 26–48 Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025 New Statistics for 2025; Updates for 2021–2024 Today, the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis released new statistics measuring the outdoor recreation economy for the nation, all 50 states, and the District of Columbia. The new data show that the value added of the outdoor recreation economy accounted for 2.3 percent ($704.2 billion) of current-dollar gross domestic product (GDP) for the nation in 2025 (national table 2). Across states and the District of Columbia, value added for outdoor recreation as a share of state GDP ranged from 6.1 percent in Hawaii to 1.0 percent in the District of Columbia (state table 1). Inflation-adjusted (“real”) GDP for the outdoor recreation economy increased 1.9 percent in 2025, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent for the overall U.S. economy, reflecting a deceleration from the 2.5 percent increase in 2024 (national table 1). In 2025, real gross output for the outdoor recreation economy increased 2.1 percent, compensation increased 4.6 percent, and employment increased 1.7 percent (national table 9). Outdoor recreation employment increased in 43 states and the District of Columbia in 2025. The change in outdoor recreation employment ranged from 5.0 percent in Rhode Island, Kansas, and the District of Columbia to −1.1 percent in New Jersey and Alabama ( BEA interactive tables ). Outdoor recreation by activity Outdoor recreation activities fall into three general categories: (1) conventional activities such as bicycling, boating, hiking, and hunting; (2) other activities such as gardening and outdoor concerts; and (3) supporting activities such as construction, travel and tourism, local trips, and government expenditures. In 2025, conventional outdoor recreation accounted for 29.2 percent of U.S. outdoor recreation value added, compared with 29.1 percent in 2024. “Other outdoor recreation” accounted for 19.3 percent of value added in 2025, compared with 19.1 percent in 2024. Supporting outdoor recreation accounted for 51.5 percent of value added in 2025, compared with 51.7 percent in 2024. Additional highlights for value added by activity for 2025 include (state table 2): Boating/fishing was the largest conventional activity for the nation at $39.1 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in 35 states and the District of Columbia. The states with the largest contributions were Florida ($4.5 billion), California ($3.3 billion), and Texas ($3.0 billion). RVing was the second-largest conventional activity for the nation at $26.8 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in 10 states. The states with the largest contributions were Indiana ($4.7 billion), Texas ($2.6 billion), and California ($2.1 billion). Hunting/shooting/trapping was the third-largest conventional activity for the nation at $15.1 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in Arizona and Wyoming. The states with the largest contributions were Texas ($1.8 billion), California ($849.8 million), and Florida ($831.3 million). Snow activities for the nation totaled $7.8 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in Colorado, Utah, and Vermont. The states with the largest contributions were Colorado ($1.8 billion), California ($735.7 million), and Utah ($640.1 million). Outdoor recreation by industry The outdoor recreation by industry data show the contributions of industries to the outdoor recreation economy, including their impact on value added, gross output, employment, and compensation. For the nation, the arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services industry group was the largest contributor to U.S. outdoor recreation in 2025, accounting for $179.5 billion, or 25.5 percent of current-dollar value added. At the state level, arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services was the largest contributor to outdoor recreation value added in 25 states and the District of Columbia. The states with the largest contributions were California ($23.5 billion), Florida ($23.4 billion), and New York ($11.6 billion) (state table 3). Retail trade was the second-largest industry group for the nation, at $166.5 billion, or 23.6 percent of value added, and was the largest industry group in 22 states. The states with the largest contributions were California ($19.5 billion), Texas ($14.6 billion), and Florida ($13.3 billion). Transportation and warehousing was the third-largest industry group for the nation, at $86.4 billion, or 12.3 percent of value added, and was the largest industry group in Alaska. The states with the largest contributions were Florida ($12.8 billion), California ($10.8 billion), and Texas ($7.1 billion). Annual update of outdoor recreation economic statistics Estimates for 2021 to 2024 were updated to incorporate newly available and revised source data. At the national level, gross output, value added, employment, and compensation reflect the results of the 2026 annual update of the National Economic Accounts, which include the National Income and Product Accounts and the Industry Economic Accounts. The state statistics now reflect these updated national data as well as the 2026 annual update of the Regional Economic Accounts and newly available and revised regional source data. Previously published estimates are available in BEA’s Data Archive . For definitions, statistical conventions, BEA regions, uses of these statistics, and more, visit " Additional Information " Next release: Fall 2027 Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2026 Full Release & Tables PDF Tables - National Level XLSX Tables - State Level XLSX Interactive State Tables Additional Information Technical Stanislaw Rzeznik (Regional) 301-278-9458 OutdoorRecreation@bea.gov Technical Connor Franks (National) 301‐278‐9710 OutdoorRecreation@bea.gov Media Connie O'Connell 301-278-9003 Connie.OConnell@bea.gov

title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
body: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now Systems from ASUS, Dell and MSI are now available — with more from Acer, GIGABYTE, HP and Microsoft on the way — bringing RTX acceleration and up to 128GB of unified memory to local AI, development and creative workflows. November 18, 2026 by Justin Walker 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops like the ASUS ProArt GR1X mini PC are built to run personal AI agents 24/7. RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage. This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including: Running massive 120-billion-parameter large language models locally Rendering 90GB+ 3D scenes in real time Smoothly editing 4:2:2 video in real time The MSI EdgeMesa N AI+ Series RTX Spark compact desktop. New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box . From Local Agents to AI Creation Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth. RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions. NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows. These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device — from isolating a subject and defining its motion to generating the finished video. NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and animations for a shared digital Miami landscape. The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark. Adobe Accelerates the Full Creative Stack for RTX Spark NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark. Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX , including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting. GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables. Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters. Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required. Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark. Blender 5.3 Adds DLSS Ray Reconstruction to the Viewport Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work. The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time. DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software. Windows Server 2028 Coming to DGX Station for Windows Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data. Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip is expanding to include support for Windows Server 2028. New accelerator platforms and the breadth of the Windows silicon ecosystem provide customers options at different capability levels and price points for advanced AI development, local inference, and agent workloads at scale. Windows ML Updates Give Developers More Options Also announced at Microsoft Ignite, developers can now bring any GGUF model from Hugging Face and run it within Windows ML using the llama.cpp backend. The DxCGC backend, now available as an experimental release, is an integration for game developers that compiles and runs machine learning models through DirectX 12, allowing them to execute AI workloads alongside graphics. Windows APIs let applications integrate platform-provided AI capabilities adding GPU support for AION Instruct and VSR. Developers can also build high-performance AI models for Windows ML using the command line interface. #ICYMI: The Latest NVIDIA Local AI Updates 🦙 llama.cpp v1.0.0 marks a major milestone for building local AI apps. The open source inference engine introduces API versioning updates, alongside expanded model support and CUDA optimizations for NVFP4 inference. Learn more . 🎉 Ricursive Intelligence introduced its first open model: Ripple-65B Preview. The full-stack AI lab builds self-improving systems by co-optimizing hardware, software and models. Ripple-65B Preview was trained on NVIDIA B300 GPUs, refined using NVIDIA Nemotron post-training datasets and runs locally on DGX Spark. Download the NVFP4 checkpoint from Hugging Face . 🤖 Runway’s Praxis-1 is a newly released 27-billion-parameter world action model that predicts video and actions together. Developers can run it locally on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, DGX Spark and DGX Station, and adapt it to their own robots, cameras and tasks with LoRA fine-tuning. Download the NVFP4 checkpoint from Hugging Face . 🛠️ NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM helps run AI models locally on DGX Spark with just a few commands. Read the technical blog , which walks through downloading Nemotron-3.5 Lightning, setting up optimized inference, testing prompts and serving the model through a local OpenAI-compatible API. Subscribe to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter . Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X , Instagram , TikTok and Facebook . See notice regarding software product information. title: Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (November 9 through November 13, 2026)
body: Press Release Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (November 9 through November 13, 2026) Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico, Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney, in conjunction with our partner agencies in the Homeland Security Task Force (“HSTF”) announce the following prosecutorial results for the week of November 9 through November 13, 2026. The HSTF is a permanent, interagency law enforcement task force created by executive order to combat transnational criminal organizations—including cartels, trafficking networks, and foreign terrorist organizations. Convictions through Guilty Pleas: On November 9, 2026, Kevin Franco-Cartagena pleaded guilty to Counts One and Two in Criminal Case 26-115.  According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and possession with intent to distribute cocaine. Defendant was arrested on December 28, 2025. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for February 8, 2025.  AUSA Pedro R. Casablanca is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 9, 2026, Patricia Ayala-Otero pleaded guilty to Count One in Criminal Case 25-307 (RAM). According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with conspiring to possess with intent to distribute 5 kilograms or more of cocaine.  Defendant was arrested on July 15, 2025. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for February 9, 2027. AUSA Antonio López is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On November 10, 2026, Julio Varela Guzmán pleaded guilty to 18 U.S.C. §§ 1956(a)(1)(B)(i) and 2, in Criminal Case 25-397 (GMM).  According to the indictment, the defendant was charged with money laundering. Defendant was arrested on September 24, 2025. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for February 10, 2027. SAUSA Cody A. McKinney is in charge of the prosecution of the case. Sentencings: On November 12, 2026, Defendant Tomás Bermúdez-Monroig, was sentenced by United States District Court Chief Judge Raúl Arias-Marxuach to 27 months of imprisonment and three years of supervised release for a conspiracy to commit bank, wire, and mail fraud. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on June 12, 2025, in Criminal Case 25-275 (RAM), and pleaded guilty on August 11, 2026. SAUSA Vanessa Bonano is in charge of the prosecution of the case. These prosecutions are part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Juan comprises agents and officers from the following federal partners: FBI, ICE-HSI, CBP (OFO, AMO and Border Patrol), the U.S. Marshals Service for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, DEA, ATF, IRS, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Department of State, and the U.S. Secret Service, the Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands HIDTA, TSA, FAA, and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The HSTF also has the following state and local law enforcement partners as participating agencies: the Puerto Rico Police Department; the San Juan, Carolina, Guaynabo, Barceloneta, and Ponce Municipal Police Departments, the Puerto Rico National Guard – Counter Drug Program; the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation; the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Service (Hacienda); the Puerto Rico Port Authority; and the Virgin Islands Police Department. ### Updated November 18, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Financial Fraud Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico U.S. Marshals Service Press Release Number: 2026-125

title: El Dorado Springs Man Sentenced to 25 Years in Prison for Receiving Child Pornography
body: Press Release El Dorado Springs Man Sentenced to 25 Years in Prison for Receiving Child Pornography Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – An El Dorado Springs, Mo., man who was convicted following a jury trial after being caught with thousands of images and videos of child pornography, was sentenced in federal court. John Fitzgerald Mullings, 54, was sentenced by Senior U.S. District Judge M. Douglas Harpool to 25 years in the Bureau of Prisons without parole, followed by a lifetime of supervised release. Mullings received a 20-year sentence for one count of receiving and distributing child pornography and an additional consecutive five-year sentence for a second count of receiving and distributing child pornography. In addition to his sentence, Mullings was ordered to pay restitution to 31 of the victims depicted in the images and videos of child pornography found on Mullings’ devices. Mullings will be required to register as a sex offender upon his release from prison and will be subject to federal and state sex offender registration requirements, which may apply throughout his life. Mullings was indicted on one count of receiving and distributing child pornography from Feb. 2, 2020, to March 2, 2021, after law enforcement received multiple reports from MeWe, Dropbox and Snapchat of Mullings uploading images and videos of child pornography to their servers. Investigators contacted Mullings at his residence on March 2, 2021. Officers seized Mullings’s cell phone, which contained 678 images and 96 videos of child pornography, including rape and/or bondage of minors. On Aug. 3, 2022, law enforcement officers executed a search warrant at Mullings’s residence (which also served as the office for his business, Steward Wrecker) in relation to an unrelated state criminal investigation. Officers seized 14 cell phones, multiple computers, laptop computers and computer tablets, as well as electronic storage devices. Investigators conducted a forensic examination of those devices and determined that 11 of those electronic devices contained child pornography. On just one of Mullings’s tablets investigators found 5,197 images and 211 videos. The files included visual depictions of sexual conduct with animals, binding and/or forced sexual contact with persons, and physical assault and deceased persons. In total, investigators found 14,249 images, and 2,054 videos of child pornography among Mullings’s devices. Also located on his devices was an electronic book titled “The Pedophile’s Handbook” and evidence that Mullings was moderated online groups dedicated to the exchange of child pornography. Mullings was charged in a superseding indictment with an additional count of receiving and distributing child pornography from March 3, 2021 to Aug. 3, 2022, based on these images and videos. Following the presentation of evidence, during a two-day trial, the jury in the U.S. District Court in Springfield, Mo., deliberated for 27 minutes before returning guilty verdicts to U.S. District Judge M. Douglas Harpool. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Stephanie L. Wan and James J. Kelleher. It was investigated by the Barry County, Missouri Sheriff’s Department, Cassville, Missouri Police Department, the El Dorado Springs, Missouri Police Department, Homeland Security Investigations, the Springfield, Missouri Police Department, and the Southwest Missouri Cyber Crimes Task Force. Project Safe Childhood This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc and click on the tab "resources." Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Missouri, Western

title: BOGALUSA WOMAN CONVICTED OF MAIL FRAUD, WIRE FRAUD, AND MONEY LAUNDERING AFTER MULTI-YEAR SCHEME TO DEFRAUD SMALL BUSINESS IN WALKER
body: Press Release BOGALUSA WOMAN CONVICTED OF MAIL FRAUD, WIRE FRAUD, AND MONEY LAUNDERING AFTER MULTI-YEAR SCHEME TO DEFRAUD SMALL BUSINESS IN WALKER Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Louisiana Tina Pierce, age 58, of Bogalusa, Louisiana, pleaded guilty to mail fraud, wire fraud, and money laundering before U.S. District Judge John W. deGravelles in connection with a multi-year scheme to defraud a small business in Walker, Louisiana. According to admissions made as part of her guilty plea, Pierce was hired in 2020 to work as the bookkeeper of a small business in Walker, Louisiana. Beginning in or about November 2020 and continuing through February 2024, Pierce executed a scheme to defraud the company and its owners using her access to the company’s books, bank account information, and accounting software. She would send payments from the company’s bank accounts to her personal bank accounts, to pay for personal purchases and charges made by her and another individual with whom she had a close relationship. Pierce would also send funds from the company’s bank accounts to a personal PayPal account maintained by one of her relatives and then cause her relative to route the funds to her. Throughout her employment, Pierce concealed her scheme in various ways.  When questioned about the transactions, she would make false statements to the company’s owners, including falsely telling them that she had “loaned” the company money and that the transactions represented “repayments” of these alleged loans, and falsely telling them that she had purchased a large insurance policy for the company and that the transactions represented premium payments for the policy. Pierce admitted in court that she caused more than 100 fraudulent transactions from the company’s business bank accounts and embezzled more than $200,000. U.S. Attorney Kurt L. Wall praised the work of the United States Secret Service. Assistant U.S. Attorney Alan A. Stevens, who serves as Senior Litigation Counsel for the Criminal Division, leads the prosecution. Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Louisiana, Middle

title: Brooksville Man Sentenced to Over 33 Years for Receiving, Distributing, and Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material
body: Press Release Brooksville Man Sentenced to Over 33 Years for Receiving, Distributing, and Possessing Child Sexual Abuse Material Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, Florida – Julian Russell Clawson (43, Tampa) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Mary Scriven sentenced to 33 years and 11 months in federal prison, followed by a lifetime of supervised release, for receiving, distributing, and possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) while on supervised release for possessing CSAM. Clawson was also ordered to pay $55,500 in restitution to victims of the offense and register as a sexual offender. A federal jury found Clawson guilty on July 14, 2026. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to testimony and evidence presented at trial, Clawson traded CSAM on a social media application (app). He engaged in graphic sexual discussions about the abuse of minors in public groups on the app, as well as with two different undercover FBI agents. As part of Clawson’s direct messages with the FBI agents, he distributed CSAM to both undercover agents on multiple dates in April 2023. Through records obtained from the social media platform, the investigation revealed Clawson had also received CSAM through this application. In June 2023, a search warrant was executed for Clawson’s cellphone revealing that he possessed more than 250 images and videos of CSAM on his phone. This case was investigated by the FBI in Sarasota and Jacksonville, the Tampa Police Department, and the Hernando County Sherriff’s Office. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Ilyssa M. Spergel. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc. Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Florida, Middle

Former Supervisory ICE Deportation Officer Sentenced To 37 Months In Prison For Bribery Conspiracy
body: Press Release Former Supervisory ICE Deportation Officer Sentenced To 37 Months In Prison For Bribery Conspiracy Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, announced today that HENRY YAU, a former supervisory deportation officer in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (“ICE”), was sentenced today to 37 months in prison for conspiring to solicit and accept bribes and gratuities.  In exchange for bribes and gratuities, YAU abused his influence and status as a supervisory deportation officer to disclose confidential law enforcement and immigration information to unauthorized recipients, provide expedited processing of foreign nationals entering the United States, tip off an individual about an ongoing investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), and arrest a particular individual (“Victim-1”) that members of a bank fraud conspiracy were seeking to silence and intimidate.  YAU previously pled guilty on March 26, 2026, before U.S. District Judge Colleen McMahon, who imposed today’s sentence. "For years, Henry Yau repeatedly abused his position of public trust as a Supervisory ICE Deportation Officer in New York City by soliciting and accepting bribes and gratuities,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. ​“Today’s sentence exemplifies the consequence awaiting law enforcement officers who sell public authority and influence for private gain.” According to the Information, court records, and statements made in Court: YAU was a Supervisory Deportation Officer with ICE, which is a law enforcement agency within the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”).  ICE’s stated mission includes protecting the U.S. through criminal investigations and enforcing immigration laws to preserve national security and public safety.  Between in or about 2016 and in or about November 2024, YAU was employed as a Deportation Officer with ICE.  In or around September 2021, YAU was promoted to Supervisory Deportation Officer.  YAU was assigned to the ICE New York Field Office, located in Manhattan.  As an ICE Deportation Officer, YAU was given access to several password-protected law enforcement databases operated by DHS and other law enforcement agencies, including U.S. Customs and Immigration Service (“USCIS”) databases containing the status of immigration-related applications filed by aliens, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (“CBP”) databases containing information about border crossings, criminal history databases containing people’s arrest and conviction records, and ICE databases containing records relating to arrests and removals of aliens from the U.S. From at least in or about 2016 through at least in or about 2024, YAU participated with others in a scheme to obtain bribes and gratuities in exchange for disseminating confidential law enforcement and immigration information, processing the entry of foreign nationals and other individuals into the United States, and arresting Victim-1 at the request of members of a bank fraud conspiracy.  The confidential information that YAU disclosed to others included confidential law information regarding the status of a pending federal investigation into a particular individual by the FBI, as well as information about the immigration status of foreign nationals and border crossing histories. In total, YAU improperly disclosed confidential law enforcement and immigration information regarding at least 28 individuals to approximately 12 co-conspirators, and he accepted over $12,000 in cash, dinners at expensive restaurants, top-shelf bottles of alcohol, and other things of value in exchange for these official acts and violations of duty. Additionally, YAU conspired to assist various foreign nationals and other bribe-payors by expediting their entry into the United States.  YAU did so by circumventing the policies and procedures at JFK Airport and arranging for these foreign nationals to get expedited entry into the United States without secondary inspections, thereby allowing these foreign nationals to be subjected to less scrutiny at the border. YAU also defrauded the Small Business Administration (“SBA”), the New York State Emergency Rental Assistance Program, and the Federal Employee Education and Assistance Fund, falsely claiming business and rental income losses relating to the COVID-19 pandemic or other natural disasters.  YAU and others also participated in a fraud on New York State Medicaid by submitting fraudulent timesheets dramatically exaggerating the number of hours spent providing home care to YAU’s elderly parents between at least in or around 2018 and in or around 2024. *                *                * In addition to the prison term, YAU, 43 of New York, New York, was sentenced to three years of supervised release and ordered to pay forfeiture of $12,600, restitution of $177,000, and a fine of $25,000. Mr. McDonald praised the outstanding work of the FBI.  Mr. McDonald also thanked CBP’s Office of Professional Responsibility, the DHS Office of Inspector General, and the New York City Department of Investigation for their assistance with the investigation This case is being handled by the Office’s Public Corruption Unit and Violent Organizations & Crime Unit.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys Andrew K. Chan, James Ligtenberg, and Ni Qian are in charge of the prosecution. Contact Nicholas Biase, Shelby Wratchford (212) 637-2600 Updated November 18, 2026 Topics Public Corruption Violent Crime Component USAO - New York, Southern Press Release Number: 26-332

title: Pharmacy Owner Sentenced to 82 Months in Prison for $5.6M Health Care Fraud Scheme and Illegal Distribution of Oxycodone
body: Press Release Pharmacy Owner Sentenced to 82 Months in Prison for $5.6M Health Care Fraud Scheme and Illegal Distribution of Oxycodone Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A Michigan pharmacy owner was sentenced yesterday to 82 months in prison with three years’ supervised release for a $5.6 million health care fraud scheme and for illegally distributing oxycodone. The defendant has been detained since October 7, after his arrest for violating his bond conditions. “Fraud against Medicare and Medicaid does not just drain taxpayer-funded programs, it shifts costs onto taxpayers, strains the health care system, and contributes to higher health care costs nationwide,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “In this case, the defendant’s scheme caused millions of dollars in losses to Medicare and Medicaid and involved the illegal diversion of thousands of oxycodone pills onto our streets, compounding the harm to the public. The Fraud Division will continue to deploy its resources to hold accountable fraudsters and drug dealers like Ali Naserdean.” “Naserdean lied to the government and cheated the American taxpayer out of millions. And that wasn’t enough,” said U.S. Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon, Jr. for the Eastern District of Michigan. “So, he turned around and poisoned the community with drugs.” “Those who choose to profit from health care fraud and the illegal distribution of opioids should expect to lose their freedom, their livelihood, and the proceeds of their crimes,” said Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Scott J. Lampert for the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “HHS-OIG and our law enforcement partners will continue to identify, investigate, and pursue individuals who endanger patients, taxpayers, and our communities.” “This defendant orchestrated a multimillion-dollar fraud scheme that stole from health care programs while illegally distributing addictive opioids into our communities. His pursuit of personal profit came at the expense of taxpayers, the integrity of our health care system, and public safety,” said Special Agent in Charge Jennifer Runyan of the FBI Detroit Field Office. “I want to recognize the outstanding work of our FBI Detroit investigators, alongside our federal law enforcement partners, as well as the Dearborn Police Department, whose persistence helped bring this case to sentencing. Anyone who believes they can exploit our health care system while fueling the illegal distribution of dangerous drugs should understand that these crimes carry serious consequences.” According to court documents, Ali Naserdean, 32, of Dearborn Heights, defrauded Medicare, Medicaid, and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan over $5.6 million stemming from his work as a pharmacy technician at three metro-Detroit pharmacies and his ownership of one of the pharmacies. From 2019 through 2022, Naserdean and his co-conspirator, pharmacist Isaiah Okoh, sent false claims to health care benefit programs for prescription drugs that were not ordered by a doctor and were not dispensed to the patient. Naserdean and Okoh used forged prescriptions from doctors to hide their scheme, when in fact the patient had never seen the listed doctor and the medication had never actually been prescribed. Additionally, from 2019 through 2022, Naserdean distributed oxycodone to drug traffickers in exchange for cash, without regard to whether the drugs were actually prescribed by physicians or dispensed in good faith. A search warrant executed at Naserdean’s residence revealed substantial evidence of his drug-dealing and fraud. Drugs Prepared for Distribution by Naserdean Cash Seized from Naserdean’s Home In April 2026, Naserdean pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit health care fraud and possession with intent to illegally distribute oxycodone. In December 2025, Naserdean’s co-conspirator, pharmacist Isaiah Okoh, was sentenced to over six years in prison . In addition to the prison sentence, the Court ordered the immediate forfeiture of money and property worth approximately $1.2 million, in addition to entering a personal money judgment against Naserdean in the amount of $5,636,721.89, and ordering restitution to the Department of Health and Human Services in the amount of $3,654,895.65 and to Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan in the amount of $21,428.93. The FBI Detroit Field Office, HHS-OIG, and the City of Dearborn Police Department investigated the case. Trial Attorney Jeffrey A. Crapko of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul A. Kuebler for the Eastern District of Michigan prosecuted the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/fraud/health-care-fraud-section . Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1375

title: Ukrainian National Charged with Illegally Voting in  2024 United States Presidential Election
body: Press Release Ukrainian National Charged with Illegally Voting in  2024 United States Presidential Election Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On November 18, 2026, Inna Opatska, age 31, a Ukrainian national of Vestal, New York, appeared on a charge of voting by an alien.  Opatska is a lawful permanent resident.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) made the announcement. According to the criminal complaint affidavit, despite lacking citizenship, Opatska voted in the federal 2024 General Election, which included election of a United States President.  The complaint also alleges that Opatska knew that she was not a United States citizen. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “To preserve and protect the integrity of American elections, we must vigorously enforce the prohibition against foreign nationals from voting in federal elections.  My office will continue to aggressively prosecute illegal voters to safeguard against foreign interference and restore the public’s confidence in our election process.” This charge carries a maximum sentence of one year in prison and a fine up to $100,000.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines, and other factors. The charges in the complaint are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Tamara Thomson and Michael Stoianoff are prosecuting the case. Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Voting and Elections Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Sioux Falls Man Sentenced to Over 20 Years in Federal Prison  for Distribution of a Controlled Substance Resulting in Death
body: Press Release Sioux Falls Man Sentenced to Over 20 Years in Federal Prison  for Distribution of a Controlled Substance Resulting in Death Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota SIOUX FALLS - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that Chief Judge Roberto A. Lange, U.S. District Court, has sentenced a Sioux Falls man convicted of Distribution of a Controlled Substance Resulting in Death.  The sentencing took place on November 16, 2026. Austin Domel, 28, was sentenced to 20 years and 10 months in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Domel was indicted for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance and Distribution of a Controlled Substance Resulting in Death by a federal grand jury in January of 2026.  He pleaded guilty on September 1, 2026. On May 20, 2025, Sioux Falls Police found a 28-year-old male deceased in his apartment. Paraphernalia found on the scene indicated a likely fentanyl overdose, and an autopsy later confirmed fentanyl toxicity as the cause of death.  Messages found on the victim’s phone showed that he had purchased fentanyl from Domel several hours before being found. “Illicit fentanyl destroys lives and decimates families,” said U.S. Attorney Parsons.  “We are doing everything we can to make it as hard as possible to obtain this toxic substance and to remove those who are selling it from our communities.” This case was investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration and the Sioux Falls Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Joyce prosecuted the case. Domel was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. Guy was also charged with two counts of possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. If convicted, Guy and Hoskins face a maximum sentence of 15 years in federal prison on each count of conspiracy to traffic firearms, conspiracy to straw purchase firearms, and possessing a firearm as a convicted felon, and a maximum sentence of 5 years’ imprisonment for the conspiracy to make a false statement offense. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to the indictment, Hoskins purchased AR-15 lower receivers from several licensed firearms dealers on behalf of Guy. Due to Guy’s prior felony convictions for aggravated battery, robbery with a firearm or deadly weapon, and burglary with assault or battery, Guy is federally prohibited from purchasing or possessing firearms under federal law. An indictment is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty. This case was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. It will be prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Simon Eth. This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. “Lows” Gang Member Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison For His Participation in a RICO Conspiracy
body: Press Release “Lows” Gang Member Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison For His Participation in a RICO Conspiracy Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal judge sentenced Deontae Jackson, 37, of Minneapolis to 10 years in prison for his role in a Racketeering Influenced Corrupt Organization (RICO) conspiracy that included violence and fentanyl distribution. Jackson is the first of 14 defendants sentenced in this case, U.S. v. Alowonle et al. (24-cr-293). According to court documents, beginning on or about 2009 and continuing through at least April 2026, Jackson was a member of and associated with the Lows gang. The Lows gang does not have a formal structure or initiation process as it is comprised of several affiliated subsets. Members would prove their loyalty by “putting in work,” which included committing acts of violence and drug trafficking. Between February 2023 and May 2024, Jackson sold fentanyl as part of, and to benefit, the Lows gang. The Lows drug trafficking activities during this period involved over 1.2 kilograms of fentanyl. On April 26, 2024, law enforcement searched a home in Fridley, Minnesota, where Jackson was staying. In Jackson’s bedroom, officers found approximately 945 M-30 fentanyl pills, which collectively weighed around 94.5 grams. At the time of the search, Jackson was on electronic court monitoring in connection with his conviction for a gang-related drive-by shooting. After the search, Jackson removed his ankle monitor to avoid having his location tracked. In May 2024, law enforcement tracked Jackson to Bismarck, North Dakota. Officers then searched Jackson’s hotel room where he was staying with a fellow Lows member and two others. Police recovered a bag containing 2,599 M-30 fentanyl pills that weighed approximately 270.4 grams. In a second bag, officers found 20 more M-30 fentanyl pills that weighed 2.08 grams. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division; Special Agent in Charge Joseph Persails of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) St. Paul Field Division; Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Kuszynski of the IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI) Chicago Field Office; Special Agent in Charge Travis Pickard of the Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) St. Paul Field Office; and Inspector in Charge Brian Musgrove of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) Denver Division made the announcement. body: Press Release Serial Armed Robber Sentenced to 30 Years in Federal Prison Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, Florida – Devon Floyd (33, Tampa) has been sentenced by U.S. District Judge Thomas P. Barber to 30 years in federal prison for robbing four convenience stores during the summer of 2023. A federal jury found Floyd guilty in July 2026. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. title: Illegal Aliens Who Burglarized Homes of Asian and Indian Families Sentenced to Federal Prison
body: Press Release Illegal Aliens Who Burglarized Homes of Asian and Indian Families Sentenced to Federal Prison Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia GAINESVILLE, Ga. – Three illegal aliens from Colombia who were previously convicted for burglarizing the homes of Asian and Indian families in Forsyth County have been sentenced to federal prison for offenses stemming from their illegal presence in the United States. “These illegal aliens disrespected our laws with their very presence and preyed upon our community when, as members of an organized burglary crew, they targeted Asian and Indian households to steal valuable items,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “Thanks to strong partnerships between federal and state law enforcement, they will be repatriated to their home country and banished from ours after serving several years in prison to pay for their crimes.” “These defendants deliberately preyed on Asian and Indian families, targeting their homes and taking advantage of the sense of security every family deserves,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “Through our strong partnerships with local, state, and federal law enforcement, we helped bring these serial burglars to justice and ensure they are held accountable for the harm they caused our communities.” “The theft and illegal sale of a loaded firearm made an already serious crime even more dangerous,” said Ryan Todd, Assistant Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Atlanta Field Division. “Through partnerships with federal, state, and local law enforcement, ATF helped hold these defendants accountable and protect our communities.” “Homeland Security Investigations remains committed to identifying and holding accountable criminal aliens who endanger the safety and security of our communities,” said Ellen Johnson, Acting Special Agent in Charge of HSI in Georgia and Alabama. “Through close coordination with our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, these repeat offenders are being held responsible for their crimes and will face removal from the United States after serving their federal sentences.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: On September 17, 2022, Luis Armando Estupinan-Cayola burglarized the home of an Asian family in Forsyth County and stole a loaded pistol, $7,000 in cash, and approximately $8,000 of jewelry. He later sold the pistol and, in February 2023, he was arrested during the burglary of another Asian family’s home. On November 2, 2022, Santi Ricardo Esteban-Delgado and Carlos Andres Perez-Melens burglarized the home of a third Asian family in Forsyth County. A month and a half later, on December 17, 2022, they burglarized the home of an Indian family. Both men were convicted of first-degree burglary in the Superior Court of Forsyth County following their arrests in 2023. Esteban-Delgado and Perez-Melens had multiple prior convictions for burglaries targeting Asian and Indian families’ homes in Georgia and other states since at least 2010. Following their state-court convictions related to these prior burglaries, Esteban-Delgado and Perez-Melens were deported from the United States. However, both defendants illegally reentered the United States prior to the 2022 burglaries. On November 16, 2026, U.S. District Judge Richard W. Story sentenced Santi Ricardo Esteban-Delgado, 41, to six years and five months in prison to be followed by three years of supervised release. Esteban-Delgado pled guilty to illegal re-entry on July 7, 2026. On August 18, 2026, Judge Story sentenced Carlos Andres Perez-Melens, 46, to five years and three months in prison to be followed by three years of supervised release. Perez-Melens pled guilty to illegal re-entry on April 27, 2026. On August 12, 2026, Judge Tiffany R. Johnson sentenced Luis Armando Estupinan-Cayola, 35, to four years and nine months in prison. Estupinan-Cayola pled guilty to illegal possession of a firearm by an alien on April 21, 2026. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Jennifer Keen prosecuted the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . title: Miami Man Charged in Account-Takeover Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Miami Man Charged in Account-Takeover Fraud Scheme Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida Coordinated arrests target fraud schemes linked to more than $54 million in losses at over 65 financial institutions MIAMI – A Miami man has been arrested on federal charges for allegedly carrying out an account-takeover fraud scheme that caused more than $600,000 in losses. His arrest was one of five coordinated arrests in Florida as part of a nationwide law enforcement effort targeting sophisticated account-takeover fraud schemes, which have been linked to more than $54 million in losses to U.S. victims at over 65 financial institutions. According to court records, Donnell Collier, Jr., 22, of Miami, allegedly perpetrated an account-takeover fraud scheme resulting in 32 outgoing wires, totaling more than $600,000. Collier is charged with wire fraud conspiracy, wire fraud, and bank fraud. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of 80 years in federal prison. Collier was among five individuals arrested during a coordinated operation involving FBI field offices in Miami, Nashville, New York, Columbia, Houston, and Omaha. Four defendants were arrested in the Southern District of Florida, while a fifth South Florida resident was arrested in the Middle District of Florida. Additional arrests and charges include: Brioden Jean and Derek Val Pierre-Paul: Charged in the Western District of Tennessee with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and two counts of wire fraud. Jean was arrested in the Southern District of Florida, while Pierre-Paul was arrested in the Middle District of Florida. Kevin Lopez and John Sardinas: Charged in the Southern District of Iowa with conspiracy to commit money laundering and four counts of money laundering. Both were arrested in the Southern District of Florida. In November 2025, the FBI released a public service announcement titled “ Account Takeover Fraud via Impersonation of Financial Institution Support ,” detailing how criminals impersonate financial institution representatives to gain access to victims’ accounts and providing guidance on how consumers can protect themselves. The public is encouraged to remain vigilant against account-takeover fraud. Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas of the Southern District of Florida and Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office made the announcement. FBI Miami is investigating the case, with assistance from the National Cyber-Forensics & Training Alliance (NCFTA) and their members. Assistant U.S. Attorney Derick Vollrath is prosecuting the case against Collier in the Southern District of Florida and coordinating the district’s involvement in the broader law enforcement operation. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.sdfl.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.sdfl.uscourts.gov , under case number 26-mj-06639. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Cybercrime Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: California Man Sentenced to 25 Years in Federal Prison  for Conspiracy to Distribute Methamphetamine
body: Press Release California Man Sentenced to 25 Years in Federal Prison  for Conspiracy to Distribute Methamphetamine Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of South Dakota SIOUX FALLS - United States Attorney Ron Parsons announced today that Chief Judge Roberto A. Lange, U.S. District Court, has sentenced a Lodi, California, man convicted of Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance. The sentencing took place on November 16, 2026. John Odom Harris, Jr., 42, was sentenced to 25 years in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release, and ordered to pay a $100 special assessment to the Federal Crime Victims Fund. Harris was indicted for Conspiracy to Distribute a Controlled Substance by a federal grand jury in November 2024. He was later found guilty following a federal jury trial in July 2026. From early 2023 to early 2024, Harris was responsible for distributing over 100 pounds of methamphetamine to a co-conspirator who re-distributed the methamphetamine to others in South Dakota.  Harris sent methamphetamine to South Dakota through the mail from California. He also provided it to a co-conspirator in California, who then transported the drugs to South Dakota via cars and trains.  Harris’s co-conspirator was caught in possession of 42 pounds of methamphetamine in January 2024 after a targeted traffic stop by the Sioux Falls Area Drug Task Force and South Dakota Highway Patrol.  To date, three other co-conspirators from the same drug trafficking organization have been convicted and sentenced in federal court on charges of Conspiracy to Distribute Methamphetamine. Marquez McGee was sentenced to 25 years in federal prison; Ashley Brown was sentenced to over 17 years in federal prison; and Travis Jones was sentenced to over 11 years in federal prison. “I’m so proud of the collective work of the Sioux Falls Area Drug Task Force, our DEA agents, and our federal prosecutors for taking down this drug trafficking organization that was specifically targeting Sioux Falls,” said U.S. Attorney Parsons.  “They are out of business for good.” This case was investigated by the Sioux Falls Area Drug Task Force and the Drug Enforcement Administration. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mark Hodges prosecuted the case. Harris was immediately remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. title: Sentencing Scheduled in Scalpa CEO's Criminal Case
body: Press Release Sentencing Scheduled in Scalpa CEO's Criminal Case Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Virginia DOJ has established a website to notify victims ABINGDON, Va. – The sentencing hearing for Bryce Cleveland, the former President and CEO of Scalpa, is set for April 9, 2027, at 11:00 a.m. before Judge Robert S. Ballou in U.S. District Court in Abingdon. Scalpa pled guilty in July 2026 to three charges related to Scalpa’s selling of skincare products that had not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Scalpa was a for-profit corporation incorporated in Arizona in 2015 that marketed and sold medical devices and drug products intended to affect the structure and function of the human body. These products included ScalpaJECT Hyaluronic Acid, Hyaluron Pen, and Scalpatox. Between 2018 and December 2020, Cleveland devised a fraudulent scheme to unlawfully enrich himself by marketing and delivering, and causing others to market and deliver, unapproved devices to customers, including ScalpaJECT Hyaluronic Acid and Hyaluron Pen, while making false representations that the devices were not subject to FDA regulation. Similarly, Cleveland introduced and delivered, and caused others to introduce and deliver, the unapproved drug “Scalpatox” into commerce. If you believe you are a victim of any of the crimes charged, please find more information at https://www.justice.gov/criminal/criminal-vns/case/united-states-v-bryce-cleveland . title: Peruvian National Sentenced in Transnational Government Imposter Scheme that Defrauded Thousands of U.S. Consumers
body: Press Release Peruvian National Sentenced in Transnational Government Imposter Scheme that Defrauded Thousands of U.S. Consumers Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Case Is Part of Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza (Alcedo), 45, of Lima, Peru, was sentenced today to eight years in prison and three years of supervised release for overseeing a years-long transnational fraud conspiracy that used government impersonation tactics to defraud thousands of consumers across the United States. “The Justice Department is protecting U.S. consumers from fraudsters no matter where those fraudsters operate,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “We will continue to work with our partners at home and abroad to ensure that those who impersonate U.S. government and court officials to steal from Americans are brought to justice.” “These criminals preyed on hardworking Americans, using fear and intimidation to steal millions of dollars. They deliberately targeted Spanish-speaking communities, impersonating government officials and threatening innocent people with arrest and legal consequences,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas for the Southern District of Florida. “Today's sentence sends a clear message: no matter where you operate, if you target Americans, we will pursue you and bring you to justice.” “Today’s sentencing of the fourteenth defendant charged in this investigation was made possible by the outstanding collaboration between Miami Division Postal Inspectors, the Justice Department, and our international partners,” said Inspector in Charge Bladismir Rojo of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) Miami Division. “Transnational criminal organizations who victimize our citizens are not beyond our reach.” According to court documents, Alcedo was the operator of a Peruvian call center that defrauded and extorted U.S. residents by falsely threatening them with arrest, court proceedings, and immigration consequences. Alcedo admitted that she owned and operated a call center in Lima, Peru, that placed unsolicited calls to Spanish-speaking consumers in the United States and falsely claimed that they had won or qualified for free products, including computer tablets and English language courses. On later calls, Alcedo and her co-conspirators falsely claimed that victims were contractually obligated to pay large sums of money to receive the products. Alcedo and her co-conspirators impersonated government officials and lawyers to intimidate victims and force them to pay. Alcedo and her co-conspirators also threatened victims with court proceedings, arrest, and other legal consequences if they did not pay. The scheme spanned several years and thousands of victims made payments to Alcedo. Collectively, the scheme was responsible for defrauding more than 30,000 Spanish-speaking residents of the United States out of $15 million. Alcedo was extradited from Peru in April 2025 and pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud in August 2026. Including today’s sentencing in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida, 14 defendants have now been convicted and sentenced in connection with this scheme. The 14 defendants include 10 Peruvian call center owner-operators and four distribution center owner-operators who processed payments, distributed products, and facilitated the fraud in the United States, and a telephone service provider who facilitated the fraud schemes across the call centers in Peru. Alcedo and many of the defendants shared strategies on how to defraud consumer victims across the United States. Alcedo is the 10 th defendant charged in this scheme to be extradited from Peru and sentenced in federal court. In 2021 and 2022, Henrry Milla, Carlos Espinoza, Jerson Renteria, Fernan Huerta, Omar Cuzcano, Evelyng Milla, and Josmell Espinoza received sentences ranging from 88 months to 110 months in prison. In 2024, Jose Alejandro Zuñiga Cano was sentenced to 98 months in prison. USPIS investigated the case. Criminal Division Senior Trial Attorney and Transnational Criminal Litigation Coordinator Phil Toomajian prosecuted the case and Assistant U.S. Attorney Annika Miranda for the Southern District of Florida is handling asset forfeiture. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs, U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida, State Department’s Diplomatic Security Service, U.S. Marshals Service, Peruvian National Prosecutor General’s Office, and Peruvian National Police provided critical assistance with the case and extradition. This case is part of efforts being undertaken by the Department of Justice Criminal Division’s Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative (CSI). The CSI is a dedicated team of prosecutors built to find scammers who prey on Americans, disrupt their networks, and hold them accountable. CSI brings together expert prosecutors from across the Criminal Division to accelerate the prosecution of cyber-enabled financial crimes, including complex frauds, government imposter schemes, romance and inheritance scams, financially motivated sextortion, lottery and sweepstakes scams, and other predatory schemes. With nationwide jurisdiction and global reach, CSI leverages every available tool to dismantle criminal operations, pursue bad actors, recover criminal proceeds, and obtain justice for victims. The Criminal Division partners with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices across the country and is a founding member of the Scam Center Strike Force. Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Fraud Components Criminal Division Criminal - Criminal White Collar and Corporate Enforcement USAO - Florida, Southern Press Release Number: 26-1377

title: Texas-Based Company Pleads Guilty to Trafficking Deadly Synthetic Opioids
body: Press Release Texas-Based Company Pleads Guilty to Trafficking Deadly Synthetic Opioids Wednesday, November 18, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A business-to-business online marketplace headquartered in Texas — eWorldTrade LLC — pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute synthetic opioids for unlawful importation into the United States and agreed to pay a criminal fine of $1,350,000 based on its ability to pay. “The Criminal Division will hold businesses accountable that facilitate the distribution of deadly drugs that put the lives of Americans at risk – just like we would any other drug dealer,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “These incredibly dangerous, illegal synthetic opioids were manufactured abroad but brought into the U.S. because of eWorldTrade. Companies who knowingly facilitate the illicit sale of controlled substances will pay the price for the Americans they put in harm’s way.” “Businesses that knowingly facilitate the online sale of synthetic opioids are no less dangerous than cartels and foreign terrorist organizations,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Michael Perez of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Nashville. “Through close coordination with our law enforcement partners domestically and abroad, HSI will continue to identify and disrupt those networks.” According to court documents, from March 2024 through March 2025, eWorldTrade offered registered users access to dozens of products through its website, including synthetic opioids such as fentanyl, carfentanil, and nitazenes. EWorldTrade knew that these products would reach the United States through its sales. Through its paid membership tiers, eWorldTrade offered customers easier access to premium suppliers of illegal drugs if they paid more to eWorldTrade, including to China-based sellers that openly offered and sold synthetic opioids through its website. The defendant admitted that its agents knowingly and intentionally facilitated prolific sales of these illicit controlled substances and others, including heroin and methamphetamine, from international sellers to potential buyers in the United States. The Justice Department reached its resolution with eWorldTrade based on several factors, including the nature and seriousness of the offense. As part of the plea, eWorldTrade has agreed to enhance its compliance and internal controls and report to the Justice Department on remediation and implementation of the compliance measures throughout the term. EWorldTrade did not make a timely and voluntary disclosure of wrongdoing, but it received credit for its acceptance of responsibility and cooperation with the investigation, including collecting, analyzing, and producing voluminous information, providing timely updates on facts learned during its internal investigation, and engaging in timely remedial measures. The court will sentence eWorldTrade on Dec. 14. The HSI Knoxville Office and the U.S. Postal Inspection Service’s Chattanooga Office investigated the case. Trial Attorneys Jayce Born and Max J. Goldman of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) are prosecuting the case. MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations. MNF’s Narcotic and Dangerous Drug Unit investigates and prosecutes the top command and control elements of international drug cartels, drug trafficking organizations, and related transnational criminal organizations. Updated November 18, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Criminal Division Criminal - Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section Press Release Number: 26-1376
